answer: A useful sybil defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, externally costly resource before it can influence shared decisions. The system assigns reputation only after the agent completes auditable tasks, then slashes the bond for provable fraud, such as submitting the same claim under many identities. An attacker can still create accounts, but each one needs fresh capital and exposes it to loss; copying names is cheap, maintaining funded identities is not. A marble, violet, or meadow-themed profile gains no extra trust: only verified work earns influence.
